title: Dua Lipa Backs Albanian Protests Against Trump-Backed Luxury Resort on Sazan Island
text:
Pop singer Dua Lipa has voiced support for environmental protests in Albania opposing a $1.6 billion resort project on Sazan Island, which is backed by Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner. Her statement has invigorated the 'flamingo revolution,' a 45-day demonstration movement concerned about ecological damage to a pristine coastal habitat.
International pop star Dua Lipa has become involved in a significant environmental controversy in Albania , using her platform to support protests against a proposed $1.6 billion luxury resort on Sazan Island.
The project, backed by Ivanka Trump and Jared Kushner, has sparked national and international debate over environmental preservation, governmental transparency, and foreign influence. Dua Lipa, 30, who is of Albanian heritage, publicly expressed her concerns on the Service95 Book Club podcast, criticizing the Albanian government's decision to alter environmental protection laws without public consultation.
Her comments have energized the so-called 'flamingo revolution,' a sustained protest movement in Tirana that has lasted over 45 days, featuring demonstrators with pink signs and inflatable flamingos to symbolize the island's unique ecosystem. The resort's plan involves developing the remote, former Soviet military base into high-end eco-homes and hotels, a vision Ivanka Trump has called 'incredible' and 'massive in scale.
' Critics argue the development would devastate a pristine coastal area that serves as a vital habitat for sea turtles, flamingos, and other endemic species. The Albanian government, led by Prime Minister Edi Rama, has steadfastly supported the project, dismissing environmental concerns, which has led to a tense standoff. At least 18 protesters were arrested earlier this month, highlighting the government's crackdown on dissent.
Dua Lipa's involvement, coming after she was spotted at the famed Electric Lady Studios in New York-a sign of her ongoing musical work-has been described by conservation leader Aleksander Trajce of the Protection and Preservation of the Natural Environment in Albania (PPNEA) as 'powerful.
' He noted that her statement has particularly inspired younger Albanians, viewing her as a global idol who validates their cause. The controversy underscores the clash between economic development and environmental stewardship in a country seeking to boost tourism while protecting its natural treasures. The island's history as a secretive Soviet military outpost adds another layer to the debate about preserving its transformed identity.
Dua Lipa's fashion choices during her studio visits-a floaty black dress with a yellow bag, and later a white dress with black boots-have been widely covered by media, but her substantive political stance has shifted the narrative toward the Albanian protest movement's core issues. The 'flamingo revolution' shows no signs of abating, with activists vowing to continue their fight against what they see as a privileged encroachment on national heritage and biodiversity.
This case also raises questions about the influence of high-profile international figures like the Trump-Kushner family in foreign development projects. The renderings for the Sazan Island project, released in 2024, depict subterranean dwellings carved into the coastline, which proponents claim minimize ecological impact.
However, opponents remain skeptical, arguing that any large-scale construction will irreparably harm the fragile Mediterranean ecosystem. The protest's longevity and Dua Lipa's endorsement have brought global attention to a local struggle, potentially altering the project's future. As the standoff continues, the world watches to see whether Albania will bow to environmental and public pressure or proceed with the ambitious, contentious resort plan
